jobs.title: Graduate Environmental Planning Consultant
jobs.description:
Location: London, Birmingham or Leicester

Start Date: September 2027

Joining Tetra Tech as a graduate is more than starting a new job – you’ll become part of our Next Gen Talent development programme, designed to support you as you build your career with us. Alongside hands-on experience and exposure to real projects, you’ll benefit from a structured programme of regular learning, training and development opportunities, helping you grow your technical and professional skills as you progress.

You’ll be supported throughout your development by experienced colleagues, giving you the opportunity to learn, build your network and develop the skills and experience needed for a successful long-term career with Tetra Tech.

Purpose & Scope of the Role

Tetra Tech Europe is an industry-leading multi-national, multi-disciplinary consultancy. Our Environmental Planning Team supports the continued growth of the UK Environment, Sustainability & Planning (ESP) team and wider business, delivering environmental co-ordination, EIA and related assessment and management work across renewables/energy, water/utilities, residential, defence, infrastructure, waste and minerals. You’ll join a team with an established workload, a strong reputation, ISEP EIA Quality Mark membership and active involvement in industry working groups, presentations and conferences.

Your Impact in this position

Working with support from senior colleagues, you’ll contribute to environmental planning, optioneering and impact assessment across a varied project portfolio. You’ll help deliver work to programme, budget and quality standards, build your skills in project management, business development and technical assessment, and produce technically robust outputs that inform responsible project decisions.

5 Core Capabilities

Project Co-ordination Support – Support project managers across multiple projects, working with teams, stakeholders and subcontractors, and helping programme site surveys.
Environmental Impact Assessment – Assist with screening, scoping, data collection, impact assessment and reporting, with working knowledge of EIA Regulations and the EIA process.
Report Writing and Communication – Prepare clear reports such as EIAs and CEMPs, present findings where needed, and review deliverables for accuracy and compliance.
Collaboration Across Disciplines – Work with colleagues in air quality, biodiversity, land use, transport and other teams to assess impacts and mitigation.
Technical Specialism Development – Build expertise in climate change, socio-economics, human health, natural capital or construction phase environmental management.

Training, Qualifications & Experience

A Bachelor’s and/or Master’s degree in Environmental Sciences, Environmental Management or a related field, plus academic and/or practical EIA experience. Knowledge of environmental laws, regulations, guidelines and the UK planning/consenting process is essential, alongside strong communication, coordination, time management, problem-solving, attention to detail and analytical skills.

Working Environment

This is a graduate role based in a supportive consultancy environment, with hybrid working available in line with team and project needs. As you develop in the role, there will be an expectation to spend more time in the office initially to support learning, collaboration and onboarding. The role may also involve occasional travel to site or other offices as required.

Application Closing Date: 31st October 2026

Assessment Centre to be held: February 2027

jobs.description:
Location - flexible

Help shape safer, compliant buildings at project-critical level. Join us as a Principal Designer Building Regulations Consultant and bring your technical expertise to complex, high-value developments.

Purpose and Scope of the Role

This role is focused on delivering Principal Designer services under the Building Regulations
for medium to large projects. Reporting to the PDBR Lead, you will provide technical oversight across the design phase, ensuring statutory compliance, robust design coordination and effective regulatory risk management.

You will work closely with clients, contractors, Registered Building Control Approvers, local authorities and multidisciplinary design teams. While a sound understanding of CDM 2015
is important, the primary focus is on Building Regulations compliance
, design review and supporting delivery within the Building Safety Act framework.

Your impact in this position

You will play a key role in helping project teams navigate complex compliance requirements from design development through to submission and approval. Your input will improve design quality, reduce regulatory risk and support clear, auditable decision-making across projects.

This is an opportunity to influence project outcomes, advise clients on statutory duties and contribute technical leadership in a specialist, fast-evolving area of the built environment.

Building Regulations Compliance

Lead Principal Designer duties under the Building Regulations on medium-to-large projects
Review designs against functional requirements and approved documents
Identify compliance issues early and help shape practical, robust solutions

Design Coordination and Risk Management

Work with architects, engineers and specialists to plan, manage and monitor compliance throughout design
Review and develop design risk assessments across multiple disciplines
Maintain a risk-based, technically sound approach to regulatory decision-making

Technical Advisory and Reporting

Produce clear compliance statements, advisory reports and application summaries
Translate complex regulations into practical guidance for clients and project teams
Support informed decision-making through high-quality technical analysis

Stakeholder Management

Liaise confidently with clients, contractors, local authorities and RBCAs
Act as a trusted point of contact on building control and compliance matters
Support the PDBR Lead in advising on duties under the Building Safety Act

Quality, Audit and Team Support

Maintain accurate compliance records, design changes and audit trails
Contribute technical guidance to junior colleagues and coordination workshops
Support best practice across building standards and secondary CDM matters

Training, Qualifications and Experience

Applicants must hold at least one of the following: Level 2 Registered Building Control Inspector
, Chartered Architect (ARB/RIBA)
or Chartered Architectural Technologist (MCIAT)
. You will bring strong experience in building regulations compliance, design review and project delivery, plus excellent technical reporting and stakeholder communication skills. Multi-disciplinary consultancy, Welsh regulations, public sector and health and safety qualifications are advantageous.

Working Environment

This role supports flexible and hybrid working
, with a mix of office, site and home-based activity depending on project needs. Travel to project meetings, local authorities and client sites will be required. Office location and expected office attendance can be tailored around the successful candidate and business requirements.

jobs.title: NetSuite Customer Success Manager
jobs.description:
About the Role

At NoBlue2, we measure success by the value our customers realise, not simply by the projects we deliver. As a Customer Success Manager, you will help customers continuously maximise the return on their NetSuite investment by identifying opportunities to improve business performance, increase automation, reduce operational friction and unlock new capabilities that support their strategic objectives. 

Working alongside the Account Management team, you will become a strategic adviser who understands each customer’s business, measures customer health, identifies commercial and operational opportunities, reduces churn risk and develops multi-year optimisation roadmaps. You will combine commercial acumen, business consulting expertise, NetSuite knowledge and AI-enabled ways of working to help customers continually evolve their ERP landscape while creating sustainable growth opportunities for NoBlue2. 

What Good Looks Like

Each strategic customer has an active, regularly reviewed Customer Value Roadmap aligned to its business goals.
Customer Health Scores improve over time, with risks identified early and proactive interventions agreed.
Optimisation opportunities are prioritised by business impact, complexity and expected return on investment.
Customers can see measurable business value from recommendations, including stronger adoption, productivity, reporting and automation.
Account Managers have clear insight to support quarterly business reviews, renewals and strategic account planning.

Responsibilities What You’ll Do

Develop and maintain customer-specific optimisation roadmaps aligned to business goals and evolving priorities.
Prioritise quick wins and longer-term transformation initiatives based on business impact, complexity and return on investment.
Align roadmaps with NetSuite product releases and review progress regularly with customers.
Partner with Account Managers so roadmaps inform quarterly business reviews, renewal discussions and strategic account planning.
Deliver customer health checks that identify system inefficiencies, under used functionality and opportunities to add value across the customer’s product stack.
Diagnose inefficiencies across finance and operational processes and identify opportunities to automate manual activity.
Recommend improvements to reporting, visibility, decision-making, user adoption and the use of NetSuite functionality.
Identify commercial opportunities where additional services or solutions will create measurable business value.
Quantify the expected business impact and return on investment of recommendations.
Develop and maintain Customer Health Scores across the managed portfolio, monitoring engagement, adoption, satisfaction and realised value.
Identify leading indicators of churn or declining engagement and recommend proactive interventions.
Track roadmap progress and value delivered, sharing clear insight with customers and internal stakeholders.
Provide guidance on relevant industry trends and the changes customers should consider.

Requirements About You

Strong NetSuite knowledge and an understanding of how ERP capability supports finance and operational processes.
Business consulting experience, with the ability to assess current-state challenges and turn them into practical, prioritised recommendations.
Commercial acumen and confidence building value cases that connect technical improvements to measurable business outcomes.
Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills, including the ability to advise senior and executive stakeholders.
Analytical and structured, with the ability to manage a customer portfolio and maintain clear roadmaps.
Proactive and curious, with a mindset focused on uncovering opportunities customers may not yet have recognised.
Comfortable working collaboratively across Account Management, Delivery, Technical and customer teams.
Interested in using AI responsibly to improve consulting quality, efficiency and knowledge sharing.

Benefits Why Join Us

This role offers the opportunity to move beyond reactive consulting and become a portfolio strategist for strategic customers. You will shape what customers should work on over the next 12 to 24 months, identify where the greatest value can be created, and help manage the risks that could prevent renewal or expansion. 
You will work at the centre of customer value, NetSuite optimisation and strategic account growth, with the scope to influence how NoBlue2 delivers continuous value management and long-term customer partnership.

About NoBlue2

We’re recognised as the EMEA NetSuite Solution Provider Partner of the Year 2026, for the second consecutive year, delivering powerful ERP solutions that drive visibility, agility, and long-term success. Our consultants work closely with clients to tailor NetSuite to their evolving needs. We’ve also developed our own IP – TaskSuite - which includes tools like TaskCollect and TaskAnalytics, designed to solve everyday business challenges. It’s ERP, elevated. 

But what truly sets NoBlue2 apart is our people and culture. We're building a business where collaboration, ingenuity and continuous learning go hand in hand. We encourage a culture of fearlessness - giving people the confidence to challenge ideas, try new approaches, learn from mistakes and push boundaries in pursuit of better outcomes for our clients. 

Join a multi-award-winning consultancy where innovation thrives, collaboration is core, and your work truly makes an impact. 

At NoBlue2, we embrace AI as a tool for innovation, efficiency and continuous learning. We believe the best results come from combining the power of AI with the expertise and judgement of our people, helping us work smarter and deliver greater value to our customers. We're looking for curious, forward-thinking individuals who are excited to use AI responsibly, challenge traditional ways of working, and continuously improve how they work. 

Benefits

Company bonus scheme, averaging 10% of salary
25 days leave (plus bank holidays) with option to buy scheme
Private healthcare – including optical and dental cashback
Enhanced pension scheme with company matching up to 5%
Life assurance at 3 x your annual salary
Discounts with Perkbox
Regular company events
Company funded training programs
Quarterly opportunity for performance-based rewards
Hybrid by default, we trust you to decide where works best for you

jobs.description:
About the Role:

Pearson Higher Education is looking for a Principal, Digital Fulfillment Transformation and Automation to help lead a critical business transformation in how we distribute and fulfill digital learning solutions through Retail, Inclusive Access and Equitable Access models.

This role will sit within the Digital Fulfillment Organization, Higher Education’s delivery team for distribution and fulfillment with channel partners. Reporting to the Lead, Customer Success for Partner Operations, you will define, design and deliver the automation that underpins Inclusive and Equitable Access. You will combine business process transformation, Salesforce workflow automation, data fluency, and Agentic AI to remove manual work, improve launch readiness, strengthen partner operations, and create scalable, trusted fulfillment processes.

What You’ll Be Responsible For:

Distribution and fulfillment:
Lead the design and delivery of automation across channel partner distribution and order-to-entitlement fulfillment — including title, price and course section adoption file exchange, product-in-use processing and flagging, and integration outreach — applying deep domain expertise to define and document the decision logic for what is automated, what is escalated and how exceptions are handled.

Delivery:
Build advanced solutions for course and campus launch readiness; including onboarding checklists, access verification, first day of class readiness and proactive issue detection so that Digital Operations Managers and IA Launch Specialists are alerted to risks rather than manually monitoring them.

Reporting and reconciliation:
Engineer the move from manual reporting to automated, self-service dashboards and scheduled partner and internal reporting covering activations, usage, returns and revenue reconciliation,partnering with our data teams to specify the underlying data transformation and to define the quality controls, metric definitions and audit trails that make those outputs trusted.

Automation and Agentic AI:
Lead complex automation and Agentic AI projects from concept to production evaluating and prototyping emerging techniques, proving value through pilots, and recommending the prioritized sequence of work and supporting business case to the Lead of Partner Operations.

Standards and reusable solutions:
Set the technical standards for how the DFO automates including authoring the reference patterns, templates, design documentation and reusable components others build from, and acting as design consultant across partner flows so that solutions are consistent, supportable and safe to scale.

Process optimization and measurable impact:
Continuously optimize live processes and instrument them against agreed KPIs — manual touches removed, cycle time, error and escalation rates, hours returned to the team and improvements to the partner, campus, faculty and student experience — with controls, rollback plans and clear process ownership documented for each change.

Mentoring and technical leadership:
Raise capability across the team by mentoring Leads, Digital Operations Managers and IA Launch Specialists, leading by example in how processes can apply automation, new methods are tested and adopted, and influencing through demonstrated expertise and innovation rather than positional authority.

What We’re Looking For:

Essential Experience, Skills and Knowledge

Business process transformation:
Significant experience mapping, redesigning and automating end-to-end operational processes, with a track record of measurable outcomes such as reduced cycle time, removed manual touches, and lower error rates.

Automation and Agentic AI:
Practical experience applying workflow automation, integration and AI or agentic tooling to operational problems, including the judgement to know when automation is the right answer.

Salesforce workflow automation:
Deep, hands-on knowledge of Salesforce workflow automation, including designing and building record-triggered and screen flows in Flow Builder, using Flow Orchestration for multistage, cross team processes with human approval steps, and applying sound practice in error handling, testing, governance and integration with upstream and downstream systems.

Data and reporting:
Strong data literacy, including defining data requirements, data quality controls and metric definitions, and partnering with data teams to deliver trusted dashboards and automated reporting.

Roadmap and delivery:
Proven ability to build a prioritized transformation roadmap, build the business case for funding, and deliver through agile or iterative delivery with clear governance and controls.

Change management:
Experience transforming roles and ways of working, including documentation, training and adoption planning, so that automation sticks and teams move to higher value work.

Stakeholder and partner management:
Confident influencing across Leads, Digital Operations Managers, technology and data teams, and external channel partners, with the credibility to align competing priorities.

Communication:
Ability to translate complex operational and technical details into clear, executive ready recommendations and to bring people with you through change.

Desirable Experience, Skills and Knowledge

Distribution and fulfillment operations:
Working knowledge of digital supply chain, order-to-access or entitlement processes within Retail, Inclusive or Equitable Access models and channel partner environments.

Customer Success practice:
Has an understanding of partner and institutional success models, with a bias toward outcomes that improve the campus experience.

Sector experience:
Background in education, publishing or courseware, or in another subscription or entitlement-based distribution business.

Why Join Us

This is an opportunity to shape the future of digital fulfillment in Higher Education by building automation, AI-enabled workflows, and scalable operational standards that directly improve the experience for partners, campuses, faculty and students. You will work in a highly collaborative environment where your expertise will influence how teams operate, how risk is detected earlier, and how fulfillment processes scale with greater speed, accuracy and confidence.

Compensation at Pearson is influenced by factors including skill set, experience, and location.

The full-time salary range for this role is $100,000 - $120,000.

This position is eligible for Pearson’s annual incentive program. Information on benefits can be found here.

Applications will be accepted through 10/9/2026. This window may be extended depending on business needs.

At Pearson, our purpose is simple: to help people realize the life they imagine through learning. We believe that every learning opportunity is a chance for a personal breakthrough. We are the world's lifelong learning company. For us, learning isn't just what we do. It's who we are. To learn more: We are Pearson.

Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, ethnicity, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, national origin, protected veteran status, disability status or any other group protected by law. We actively seek qualified candidates who are protected veterans and individuals with disabilities as defined under VEVRAA and Section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act.

About the job

The Role

As a Customer Success Manager, the job is simple to state and hard to execute: get customers sending direct mail, fast, and keep finding new ways to help them grow their program and see real results. This role owns the full post-sale journey (onboarding, activation, and growth) for a book of business, removing the technical and organizational blockers that keep a customer from mailing and building the habits that keep them engaged and consistently seeing value.
Turn every new customer into an active, growing user of LettrLabs, someone who's consistently mailing and seeing real results. Every customer who signs with LettrLabs has committed to a monthly direct mail budget, and the job is to get them live as quickly as possible, keep them consistently active, and help them grow their campaigns. Success is measured in activation, usage, and speed to first value, not just relationship health.

Why Join Us

Success in This Role Looks Like:

Usage:
Keep the managed group of customers highly utilized, meaning a high percentage are actively using the product (sending direct mail) in any given month.
Expansion:
Help a growing share of customers expand their program over time, so usage and results grow well beyond where they started.
Time to Value:
Minimize the time from signature to live, tracked against three milestones: integration setup, automated campaign setup, and first direct mail sent.
Advocacy:
Build customer champions willing to provide references and feedback as accounts see measurable ROI.

What You Will Own

Drive Activation & Usage

Monitor engagement across the portfolio against a utilization goal; proactively identify dormant or at-risk accounts and re-engage them before they go inactive.
Own the levers that drive sending: automations, audience/list setup, tracking, and suppression, and make sure customers are actually using them.
Diagnose why an account isn't mailing (technical, workflow, or buy-in issues) and clear the path to get them sending again.

Accelerate Time to Value

Own onboarding execution against the three core milestones: integration setup, automated campaign setup, and first direct mail send.
Build and continuously improve repeatable onboarding playbooks, and hold customers accountable to a clear, mutually agreed launch timeline.
Identify and resolve technical or process blockers (data feeds, integrations, creative approvals) that delay a customer's start.

Expand Usage & Impact

Help customers scale send volume beyond their contracted monthly commitment through expanded use cases, list growth, and increased campaign cadence.
Partner with Sales to spot and act on upsell and cross-sell opportunities as soon as usage trends signal a customer is ready to expand.
Track book-of-business performance against contracted value and flag underperforming accounts early, with a plan to close the gap.

Manage Account Health & Risk

Maintain a structured, usage-based health scoring system, rooted in activation, expansion signals, and milestone completion, to catch at-risk accounts before they churn.
Build and maintain account-specific success plans tied directly to activation, expansion, and time-to-value targets, and evolve them as customer priorities shift.
Escalate systemic or recurring blockers to product, ops, and data teams, and drive them to resolution.

Cross-Functional Execution

Coordinate across product, design, ops, and data teams to remove technical or workflow barriers standing between a customer and their next send.
Communicate clearly and tactfully across internal and customer stakeholders, prioritizing competing demands without losing sight of the activation goal.

Use Claude and other AI tools daily to work faster: surfacing usage trends, drafting customer communications, and generating reports.
Bring a work smarter, not harder mindset to onboarding, account management, and reporting workflows.

5-8 years in Customer Success, Onboarding, or Account Management with full life-cycle ownership (onboarding, activation, renewals).

Proven ability to run onboarding with urgency: setting timelines, holding customers accountable, and unblocking technical issues without waiting on someone else.
High emotional intelligence with excellent interpersonal and communication skills across stakeholder levels.

Proven ability to prioritize, manage deadlines, and push back with professionalism.
Comfortable navigating ambiguity and change in a startup environment.
Resilient, action-oriented, and thrives under pressure.

Working knowledge of system integrations, including Zapier, webhooks, and cross-platform workflows.

jobs.description:
About the Role:

Pearson Higher Education is looking for a Principal, Digital Fulfillment Transformation and Automation to help lead a critical business transformation in how we distribute and fulfill digital learning solutions through Retail, Inclusive Access and Equitable Access models.

This role will sit within the Digital Fulfillment Organization, Higher Education’s delivery team for distribution and fulfillment with channel partners. Reporting to the Lead, Customer Success for Partner Operations, you will define, design and deliver the automation that underpins Inclusive and Equitable Access. You will combine business process transformation, Salesforce workflow automation, data fluency, and Agentic AI to remove manual work, improve launch readiness, strengthen partner operations, and create scalable, trusted fulfillment processes.

What You’ll Be Responsible For:

Distribution and fulfillment:
Lead the design and delivery of automation across channel partner distribution and order-to-entitlement fulfillment — including title, price and course section adoption file exchange, product-in-use processing and flagging, and integration outreach — applying deep domain expertise to define and document the decision logic for what is automated, what is escalated and how exceptions are handled.

Delivery:
Build advanced solutions for course and campus launch readiness; including onboarding checklists, access verification, first day of class readiness and proactive issue detection so that Digital Operations Managers and IA Launch Specialists are alerted to risks rather than manually monitoring them.

Reporting and reconciliation:
Engineer the move from manual reporting to automated, self-service dashboards and scheduled partner and internal reporting covering activations, usage, returns and revenue reconciliation,partnering with our data teams to specify the underlying data transformation and to define the quality controls, metric definitions and audit trails that make those outputs trusted.

Automation and Agentic AI:
Lead complex automation and Agentic AI projects from concept to production evaluating and prototyping emerging techniques, proving value through pilots, and recommending the prioritized sequence of work and supporting business case to the Lead of Partner Operations.

Standards and reusable solutions:
Set the technical standards for how the DFO automates including authoring the reference patterns, templates, design documentation and reusable components others build from, and acting as design consultant across partner flows so that solutions are consistent, supportable and safe to scale.

Process optimization and measurable impact:
Continuously optimize live processes and instrument them against agreed KPIs — manual touches removed, cycle time, error and escalation rates, hours returned to the team and improvements to the partner, campus, faculty and student experience — with controls, rollback plans and clear process ownership documented for each change.

Mentoring and technical leadership:
Raise capability across the team by mentoring Leads, Digital Operations Managers and IA Launch Specialists, leading by example in how processes can apply automation, new methods are tested and adopted, and influencing through demonstrated expertise and innovation rather than positional authority.

What We’re Looking For:

Essential Experience, Skills and Knowledge

Business process transformation:
Significant experience mapping, redesigning and automating end-to-end operational processes, with a track record of measurable outcomes such as reduced cycle time, removed manual touches, and lower error rates.

Automation and Agentic AI:
Practical experience applying workflow automation, integration and AI or agentic tooling to operational problems, including the judgement to know when automation is the right answer.

Salesforce workflow automation:
Deep, hands-on knowledge of Salesforce workflow automation, including designing and building record-triggered and screen flows in Flow Builder, using Flow Orchestration for multistage, cross team processes with human approval steps, and applying sound practice in error handling, testing, governance and integration with upstream and downstream systems.

Data and reporting:
Strong data literacy, including defining data requirements, data quality controls and metric definitions, and partnering with data teams to deliver trusted dashboards and automated reporting.

Roadmap and delivery:
Proven ability to build a prioritized transformation roadmap, build the business case for funding, and deliver through agile or iterative delivery with clear governance and controls.

Change management:
Experience transforming roles and ways of working, including documentation, training and adoption planning, so that automation sticks and teams move to higher value work.

Stakeholder and partner management:
Confident influencing across Leads, Digital Operations Managers, technology and data teams, and external channel partners, with the credibility to align competing priorities.

Communication:
Ability to translate complex operational and technical details into clear, executive ready recommendations and to bring people with you through change.

Desirable Experience, Skills and Knowledge

Distribution and fulfillment operations:
Working knowledge of digital supply chain, order-to-access or entitlement processes within Retail, Inclusive or Equitable Access models and channel partner environments.

Customer Success practice:
Has an understanding of partner and institutional success models, with a bias toward outcomes that improve the campus experience.

Sector experience:
Background in education, publishing or courseware, or in another subscription or entitlement-based distribution business.

Why Join Us

This is an opportunity to shape the future of digital fulfillment in Higher Education by building automation, AI-enabled workflows, and scalable operational standards that directly improve the experience for partners, campuses, faculty and students. You will work in a highly collaborative environment where your expertise will influence how teams operate, how risk is detected earlier, and how fulfillment processes scale with greater speed, accuracy and confidence.

Compensation at Pearson is influenced by factors including skill set, experience, and location.

The full-time salary range for this role is $100,000 - $120,000.

This position is eligible for Pearson’s annual incentive program. Information on benefits can be found here.

Applications will be accepted through 10/9/2026. This window may be extended depending on business needs.

Who we are:

At Pearson, our purpose is simple: to help people realize the life they imagine through learning. We believe that every learning opportunity is a chance for a personal breakthrough. We are the world's lifelong learning company. For us, learning isn't just what we do. It's who we are. To learn more: We are Pearson.

new_jobs.description:
Location: London, Birmingham or Leicester

Start Date: September 2027

Joining Tetra Tech as a graduate is more than starting a new job – you’ll become part of our Next Gen Talent development programme, designed to support you as you build your career with us. Alongside hands-on experience and exposure to real projects, you’ll benefit from a structured programme of regular learning, training and development opportunities, helping you grow your technical and professional skills as you progress.

You’ll be supported throughout your development by experienced colleagues, giving you the opportunity to learn, build your network and develop the skills and experience needed for a successful long-term career with Tetra Tech.

Purpose & Scope of the Role

Tetra Tech Europe is an industry-leading multi-national, multi-disciplinary consultancy. Our Environmental Planning Team supports the continued growth of the UK Environment, Sustainability & Planning (ESP) team and wider business, delivering environmental co-ordination, EIA and related assessment and management work across renewables/energy, water/utilities, residential, defence, infrastructure, waste and minerals. You’ll join a team with an established workload, a strong reputation, ISEP EIA Quality Mark membership and active involvement in industry working groups, presentations and conferences.

Your Impact in this position

Working with support from senior colleagues, you’ll contribute to environmental planning, optioneering and impact assessment across a varied project portfolio. You’ll help deliver work to programme, budget and quality standards, build your skills in project management, business development and technical assessment, and produce technically robust outputs that inform responsible project decisions.

5 Core Capabilities

Project Co-ordination Support – Support project managers across multiple projects, working with teams, stakeholders and subcontractors, and helping programme site surveys.
Environmental Impact Assessment – Assist with screening, scoping, data collection, impact assessment and reporting, with working knowledge of EIA Regulations and the EIA process.
Report Writing and Communication – Prepare clear reports such as EIAs and CEMPs, present findings where needed, and review deliverables for accuracy and compliance.
Collaboration Across Disciplines – Work with colleagues in air quality, biodiversity, land use, transport and other teams to assess impacts and mitigation.
Technical Specialism Development – Build expertise in climate change, socio-economics, human health, natural capital or construction phase environmental management.

Training, Qualifications & Experience

A Bachelor’s and/or Master’s degree in Environmental Sciences, Environmental Management or a related field, plus academic and/or practical EIA experience. Knowledge of environmental laws, regulations, guidelines and the UK planning/consenting process is essential, alongside strong communication, coordination, time management, problem-solving, attention to detail and analytical skills.

Working Environment

This is a graduate role based in a supportive consultancy environment, with hybrid working available in line with team and project needs. As you develop in the role, there will be an expectation to spend more time in the office initially to support learning, collaboration and onboarding. The role may also involve occasional travel to site or other offices as required.

Assessment Centre to be held: February 2027

new_jobs.description:
About the Role

At NoBlue2, we measure success by the value our customers realise, not simply by the projects we deliver. As a Customer Success Manager, you will help customers continuously maximise the return on their NetSuite investment by identifying opportunities to improve business performance, increase automation, reduce operational friction and unlock new capabilities that support their strategic objectives. 

Working alongside the Account Management team, you will become a strategic adviser who understands each customer’s business, measures customer health, identifies commercial and operational opportunities, reduces churn risk and develops multi-year optimisation roadmaps. You will combine commercial acumen, business consulting expertise, NetSuite knowledge and AI-enabled ways of working to help customers continually evolve their ERP landscape while creating sustainable growth opportunities for NoBlue2. 

What Good Looks Like

Each strategic customer has an active, regularly reviewed Customer Value Roadmap aligned to its business goals.
Customer Health Scores improve over time, with risks identified early and proactive interventions agreed.
Optimisation opportunities are prioritised by business impact, complexity and expected return on investment.
Customers can see measurable business value from recommendations, including stronger adoption, productivity, reporting and automation.
Account Managers have clear insight to support quarterly business reviews, renewals and strategic account planning.

Responsibilities What You’ll Do

Develop and maintain customer-specific optimisation roadmaps aligned to business goals and evolving priorities.
Prioritise quick wins and longer-term transformation initiatives based on business impact, complexity and return on investment.
Align roadmaps with NetSuite product releases and review progress regularly with customers.
Partner with Account Managers so roadmaps inform quarterly business reviews, renewal discussions and strategic account planning.
Deliver customer health checks that identify system inefficiencies, under used functionality and opportunities to add value across the customer’s product stack.
Diagnose inefficiencies across finance and operational processes and identify opportunities to automate manual activity.
Recommend improvements to reporting, visibility, decision-making, user adoption and the use of NetSuite functionality.
Identify commercial opportunities where additional services or solutions will create measurable business value.
Quantify the expected business impact and return on investment of recommendations.
Develop and maintain Customer Health Scores across the managed portfolio, monitoring engagement, adoption, satisfaction and realised value.
Identify leading indicators of churn or declining engagement and recommend proactive interventions.
Track roadmap progress and value delivered, sharing clear insight with customers and internal stakeholders.
Provide guidance on relevant industry trends and the changes customers should consider.

Requirements About You

Strong NetSuite knowledge and an understanding of how ERP capability supports finance and operational processes.
Business consulting experience, with the ability to assess current-state challenges and turn them into practical, prioritised recommendations.
Commercial acumen and confidence building value cases that connect technical improvements to measurable business outcomes.
Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills, including the ability to advise senior and executive stakeholders.
Analytical and structured, with the ability to manage a customer portfolio and maintain clear roadmaps.
Proactive and curious, with a mindset focused on uncovering opportunities customers may not yet have recognised.
Comfortable working collaboratively across Account Management, Delivery, Technical and customer teams.
Interested in using AI responsibly to improve consulting quality, efficiency and knowledge sharing.

Benefits Why Join Us

This role offers the opportunity to move beyond reactive consulting and become a portfolio strategist for strategic customers. You will shape what customers should work on over the next 12 to 24 months, identify where the greatest value can be created, and help manage the risks that could prevent renewal or expansion. 
You will work at the centre of customer value, NetSuite optimisation and strategic account growth, with the scope to influence how NoBlue2 delivers continuous value management and long-term customer partnership.

About NoBlue2

We’re recognised as the EMEA NetSuite Solution Provider Partner of the Year 2026, for the second consecutive year, delivering powerful ERP solutions that drive visibility, agility, and long-term success. Our consultants work closely with clients to tailor NetSuite to their evolving needs. We’ve also developed our own IP – TaskSuite - which includes tools like TaskCollect and TaskAnalytics, designed to solve everyday business challenges. It’s ERP, elevated. 

But what truly sets NoBlue2 apart is our people and culture. We're building a business where collaboration, ingenuity and continuous learning go hand in hand. We encourage a culture of fearlessness - giving people the confidence to challenge ideas, try new approaches, learn from mistakes and push boundaries in pursuit of better outcomes for our clients. 

Join a multi-award-winning consultancy where innovation thrives, collaboration is core, and your work truly makes an impact. 

At NoBlue2, we embrace AI as a tool for innovation, efficiency and continuous learning. We believe the best results come from combining the power of AI with the expertise and judgement of our people, helping us work smarter and deliver greater value to our customers. We're looking for curious, forward-thinking individuals who are excited to use AI responsibly, challenge traditional ways of working, and continuously improve how they work. 

Benefits

Company bonus scheme, averaging 10% of salary
25 days leave (plus bank holidays) with option to buy scheme
Private healthcare – including optical and dental cashback
Enhanced pension scheme with company matching up to 5%
Life assurance at 3 x your annual salary
Discounts with Perkbox
Regular company events
Company funded training programs
Quarterly opportunity for performance-based rewards
Hybrid by default, we trust you to decide where works best for you

About the Role:

Pearson Higher Education is looking for a Principal, Digital Fulfillment Transformation and Automation to help lead a critical business transformation in how we distribute and fulfill digital learning solutions through Retail, Inclusive Access and Equitable Access models.

This role will sit within the Digital Fulfillment Organization, Higher Education’s delivery team for distribution and fulfillment with channel partners. Reporting to the Lead, Customer Success for Partner Operations, you will define, design and deliver the automation that underpins Inclusive and Equitable Access. You will combine business process transformation, Salesforce workflow automation, data fluency, and Agentic AI to remove manual work, improve launch readiness, strengthen partner operations, and create scalable, trusted fulfillment processes.

What You’ll Be Responsible For:

Distribution and fulfillment:
Lead the design and delivery of automation across channel partner distribution and order-to-entitlement fulfillment — including title, price and course section adoption file exchange, product-in-use processing and flagging, and integration outreach — applying deep domain expertise to define and document the decision logic for what is automated, what is escalated and how exceptions are handled.

Delivery:
Build advanced solutions for course and campus launch readiness; including onboarding checklists, access verification, first day of class readiness and proactive issue detection so that Digital Operations Managers and IA Launch Specialists are alerted to risks rather than manually monitoring them.

Reporting and reconciliation:
Engineer the move from manual reporting to automated, self-service dashboards and scheduled partner and internal reporting covering activations, usage, returns and revenue reconciliation,partnering with our data teams to specify the underlying data transformation and to define the quality controls, metric definitions and audit trails that make those outputs trusted.

Automation and Agentic AI:
Lead complex automation and Agentic AI projects from concept to production evaluating and prototyping emerging techniques, proving value through pilots, and recommending the prioritized sequence of work and supporting business case to the Lead of Partner Operations.

Standards and reusable solutions:
Set the technical standards for how the DFO automates including authoring the reference patterns, templates, design documentation and reusable components others build from, and acting as design consultant across partner flows so that solutions are consistent, supportable and safe to scale.

Process optimization and measurable impact:
Continuously optimize live processes and instrument them against agreed KPIs — manual touches removed, cycle time, error and escalation rates, hours returned to the team and improvements to the partner, campus, faculty and student experience — with controls, rollback plans and clear process ownership documented for each change.

Mentoring and technical leadership:
Raise capability across the team by mentoring Leads, Digital Operations Managers and IA Launch Specialists, leading by example in how processes can apply automation, new methods are tested and adopted, and influencing through demonstrated expertise and innovation rather than positional authority.

What We’re Looking For:

Essential Experience, Skills and Knowledge

Business process transformation:
Significant experience mapping, redesigning and automating end-to-end operational processes, with a track record of measurable outcomes such as reduced cycle time, removed manual touches, and lower error rates.

Automation and Agentic AI:
Practical experience applying workflow automation, integration and AI or agentic tooling to operational problems, including the judgement to know when automation is the right answer.

Salesforce workflow automation:
Deep, hands-on knowledge of Salesforce workflow automation, including designing and building record-triggered and screen flows in Flow Builder, using Flow Orchestration for multistage, cross team processes with human approval steps, and applying sound practice in error handling, testing, governance and integration with upstream and downstream systems.

Data and reporting:
Strong data literacy, including defining data requirements, data quality controls and metric definitions, and partnering with data teams to deliver trusted dashboards and automated reporting.

Roadmap and delivery:
Proven ability to build a prioritized transformation roadmap, build the business case for funding, and deliver through agile or iterative delivery with clear governance and controls.

Change management:
Experience transforming roles and ways of working, including documentation, training and adoption planning, so that automation sticks and teams move to higher value work.

Stakeholder and partner management:
Confident influencing across Leads, Digital Operations Managers, technology and data teams, and external channel partners, with the credibility to align competing priorities.

Communication:
Ability to translate complex operational and technical details into clear, executive ready recommendations and to bring people with you through change.

Desirable Experience, Skills and Knowledge

Distribution and fulfillment operations:
Working knowledge of digital supply chain, order-to-access or entitlement processes within Retail, Inclusive or Equitable Access models and channel partner environments.

Customer Success practice:
Has an understanding of partner and institutional success models, with a bias toward outcomes that improve the campus experience.

Sector experience:
Background in education, publishing or courseware, or in another subscription or entitlement-based distribution business.

Why Join Us

This is an opportunity to shape the future of digital fulfillment in Higher Education by building automation, AI-enabled workflows, and scalable operational standards that directly improve the experience for partners, campuses, faculty and students. You will work in a highly collaborative environment where your expertise will influence how teams operate, how risk is detected earlier, and how fulfillment processes scale with greater speed, accuracy and confidence.

Compensation at Pearson is influenced by factors including skill set, experience, and location.

The full-time salary range for this role is $100,000 - $120,000.

This position is eligible for Pearson’s annual incentive program. Information on benefits can be found here.

About the job

The Role

As a Customer Success Manager, the job is simple to state and hard to execute: get customers sending direct mail, fast, and keep finding new ways to help them grow their program and see real results. This role owns the full post-sale journey (onboarding, activation, and growth) for a book of business, removing the technical and organizational blockers that keep a customer from mailing and building the habits that keep them engaged and consistently seeing value.
Turn every new customer into an active, growing user of LettrLabs, someone who's consistently mailing and seeing real results. Every customer who signs with LettrLabs has committed to a monthly direct mail budget, and the job is to get them live as quickly as possible, keep them consistently active, and help them grow their campaigns. Success is measured in activation, usage, and speed to first value, not just relationship health.

Why Join Us

Success in This Role Looks Like:

Usage:
Keep the managed group of customers highly utilized, meaning a high percentage are actively using the product (sending direct mail) in any given month.
Expansion:
Help a growing share of customers expand their program over time, so usage and results grow well beyond where they started.
Time to Value:
Minimize the time from signature to live, tracked against three milestones: integration setup, automated campaign setup, and first direct mail sent.
Advocacy:
Build customer champions willing to provide references and feedback as accounts see measurable ROI.

What You Will Own

Drive Activation & Usage

Monitor engagement across the portfolio against a utilization goal; proactively identify dormant or at-risk accounts and re-engage them before they go inactive.
Own the levers that drive sending: automations, audience/list setup, tracking, and suppression, and make sure customers are actually using them.
Diagnose why an account isn't mailing (technical, workflow, or buy-in issues) and clear the path to get them sending again.

Accelerate Time to Value

Own onboarding execution against the three core milestones: integration setup, automated campaign setup, and first direct mail send.
Build and continuously improve repeatable onboarding playbooks, and hold customers accountable to a clear, mutually agreed launch timeline.
Identify and resolve technical or process blockers (data feeds, integrations, creative approvals) that delay a customer's start.

Expand Usage & Impact

Help customers scale send volume beyond their contracted monthly commitment through expanded use cases, list growth, and increased campaign cadence.
Partner with Sales to spot and act on upsell and cross-sell opportunities as soon as usage trends signal a customer is ready to expand.
Track book-of-business performance against contracted value and flag underperforming accounts early, with a plan to close the gap.

Manage Account Health & Risk

Maintain a structured, usage-based health scoring system, rooted in activation, expansion signals, and milestone completion, to catch at-risk accounts before they churn.
Build and maintain account-specific success plans tied directly to activation, expansion, and time-to-value targets, and evolve them as customer priorities shift.
Escalate systemic or recurring blockers to product, ops, and data teams, and drive them to resolution.

Cross-Functional Execution

Coordinate across product, design, ops, and data teams to remove technical or workflow barriers standing between a customer and their next send.
Communicate clearly and tactfully across internal and customer stakeholders, prioritizing competing demands without losing sight of the activation goal.

Leverage AI & Operational Tools

Use Claude and other AI tools daily to work faster: surfacing usage trends, drafting customer communications, and generating reports.
Bring a work smarter, not harder mindset to onboarding, account management, and reporting workflows.

What You Bring

Ideal Candidate Profile

5-8 years in Customer Success, Onboarding, or Account Management with full life-cycle ownership (onboarding, activation, renewals).
A track record of hitting usage, adoption, or activation-style metrics, not just relationship or satisfaction scores.
Proven ability to run onboarding with urgency: setting timelines, holding customers accountable, and unblocking technical issues without waiting on someone else.
High emotional intelligence with excellent interpersonal and communication skills across stakeholder levels.
Familiarity with marketing automation or SaaS platforms.
Proven ability to prioritize, manage deadlines, and push back with professionalism.
Comfortable navigating ambiguity and change in a startup environment.
Resilient, action-oriented, and thrives under pressure.

Technical & Systems Expertise

Working knowledge of system integrations, including Zapier, webhooks, and cross-platform workflows.
Proficient or expert-level in Google Workspace tools (Docs, Sheets, Slides), including manipulating large datasets and generating dashboards/pivot tables.
Understands how data flows through CRMs like HubSpot and Salesforce, and can operate within those systems.
Comfortable with key SaaS and marketing automation platforms like Shopify and Klaviyo.
Understands how systems talk to each other (API logic, data flow mapping) well enough to diagnose integration issues that block activation.
Uses AI tools like Claude daily to streamline work, and ideally can help teach the team how to get more from them.

new_jobs.title: Principal, Customer Success (Digital Fulfillment Transformation & Automation)
new_jobs.description:
About the Role:

Pearson Higher Education is looking for a Principal, Digital Fulfillment Transformation and Automation to help lead a critical business transformation in how we distribute and fulfill digital learning solutions through Retail, Inclusive Access and Equitable Access models.

This role will sit within the Digital Fulfillment Organization, Higher Education’s delivery team for distribution and fulfillment with channel partners. Reporting to the Lead, Customer Success for Partner Operations, you will define, design and deliver the automation that underpins Inclusive and Equitable Access. You will combine business process transformation, Salesforce workflow automation, data fluency, and Agentic AI to remove manual work, improve launch readiness, strengthen partner operations, and create scalable, trusted fulfillment processes.

What You’ll Be Responsible For:

Distribution and fulfillment:
Lead the design and delivery of automation across channel partner distribution and order-to-entitlement fulfillment — including title, price and course section adoption file exchange, product-in-use processing and flagging, and integration outreach — applying deep domain expertise to define and document the decision logic for what is automated, what is escalated and how exceptions are handled.

Delivery:
Build advanced solutions for course and campus launch readiness; including onboarding checklists, access verification, first day of class readiness and proactive issue detection so that Digital Operations Managers and IA Launch Specialists are alerted to risks rather than manually monitoring them.

Reporting and reconciliation:
Engineer the move from manual reporting to automated, self-service dashboards and scheduled partner and internal reporting covering activations, usage, returns and revenue reconciliation,partnering with our data teams to specify the underlying data transformation and to define the quality controls, metric definitions and audit trails that make those outputs trusted.

Automation and Agentic AI:
Lead complex automation and Agentic AI projects from concept to production evaluating and prototyping emerging techniques, proving value through pilots, and recommending the prioritized sequence of work and supporting business case to the Lead of Partner Operations.

Standards and reusable solutions:
Set the technical standards for how the DFO automates including authoring the reference patterns, templates, design documentation and reusable components others build from, and acting as design consultant across partner flows so that solutions are consistent, supportable and safe to scale.

Process optimization and measurable impact:
Continuously optimize live processes and instrument them against agreed KPIs — manual touches removed, cycle time, error and escalation rates, hours returned to the team and improvements to the partner, campus, faculty and student experience — with controls, rollback plans and clear process ownership documented for each change.

Mentoring and technical leadership:
Raise capability across the team by mentoring Leads, Digital Operations Managers and IA Launch Specialists, leading by example in how processes can apply automation, new methods are tested and adopted, and influencing through demonstrated expertise and innovation rather than positional authority.

What We’re Looking For:

Essential Experience, Skills and Knowledge

Business process transformation:
Significant experience mapping, redesigning and automating end-to-end operational processes, with a track record of measurable outcomes such as reduced cycle time, removed manual touches, and lower error rates.

Automation and Agentic AI:
Practical experience applying workflow automation, integration and AI or agentic tooling to operational problems, including the judgement to know when automation is the right answer.

Salesforce workflow automation:
Deep, hands-on knowledge of Salesforce workflow automation, including designing and building record-triggered and screen flows in Flow Builder, using Flow Orchestration for multistage, cross team processes with human approval steps, and applying sound practice in error handling, testing, governance and integration with upstream and downstream systems.

Data and reporting:
Strong data literacy, including defining data requirements, data quality controls and metric definitions, and partnering with data teams to deliver trusted dashboards and automated reporting.

Roadmap and delivery:
Proven ability to build a prioritized transformation roadmap, build the business case for funding, and deliver through agile or iterative delivery with clear governance and controls.

Change management:
Experience transforming roles and ways of working, including documentation, training and adoption planning, so that automation sticks and teams move to higher value work.

Stakeholder and partner management:
Confident influencing across Leads, Digital Operations Managers, technology and data teams, and external channel partners, with the credibility to align competing priorities.

Communication:
Ability to translate complex operational and technical details into clear, executive ready recommendations and to bring people with you through change.

Desirable Experience, Skills and Knowledge

Distribution and fulfillment operations:
Working knowledge of digital supply chain, order-to-access or entitlement processes within Retail, Inclusive or Equitable Access models and channel partner environments.

Customer Success practice:
Has an understanding of partner and institutional success models, with a bias toward outcomes that improve the campus experience.

Sector experience:
Background in education, publishing or courseware, or in another subscription or entitlement-based distribution business.

Why Join Us

This is an opportunity to shape the future of digital fulfillment in Higher Education by building automation, AI-enabled workflows, and scalable operational standards that directly improve the experience for partners, campuses, faculty and students. You will work in a highly collaborative environment where your expertise will influence how teams operate, how risk is detected earlier, and how fulfillment processes scale with greater speed, accuracy and confidence.

Compensation at Pearson is influenced by factors including skill set, experience, and location.

The full-time salary range for this role is $100,000 - $120,000.

This position is eligible for Pearson’s annual incentive program. Information on benefits can be found here.

Applications will be accepted through 10/9/2026. This window may be extended depending on business needs.

Who we are:

At Pearson, our purpose is simple: to help people realize the life they imagine through learning. We believe that every learning opportunity is a chance for a personal breakthrough. We are the world's lifelong learning company. For us, learning isn't just what we do. It's who we are. To learn more: We are Pearson.
